purpose: Explain selection scope, conversation overlap and count-versus-byte arithmetic without connecting an account.
assumptions: All addresses use reserved example.com domains. No real mailbox data.
Date comparisons are ISO calendar dates in this model, with before strictly exclusive; no Gmail timezone equivalence is asserted.
Queries below are explanatory strings, not parsed by this fixture file. Matching predicates are explicitly stated.
A conversation is included when any single message satisfies the stated predicate. Displayed conversation IDs do not establish action scope or exact Gmail counters.
Sender-wide scope is modeled as the union of conversations containing a selected sender, excluding Spam and Trash; actual Gmail aliases, threading and UI behavior require external observation.
Size examples sum declared decimal KB without MIME, attachment encoding, account quota overhead or deduplication. They are not quota forecasts.

sources.supports: Negative operators can return a conversation containing excluded messages; date, size and sender query syntax.
Selection and Gmail Trash recovery procedures; does not validate this model.

fixtures.intent: Keep a recent starred reply while finding old newsletters
fixtures.predicate: from == news@example.com AND date < 2025-01-01 AND starred == false
fixtures.teaches: A result conversation can contain both matching and excluded messages. Inspect a mixed thread and action scope.

fixtures.intent: Show that category/date restrictions are not inherited by the extension
fixtures.prior_predicate: from == shop@example.com AND category == promotions AND date < 2025-01-01 AND starred == false
fixtures.extension_predicate: from is selected AND folder not in [spam, trash]
fixtures.teaches: An archived recent starred receipt remains in sender-wide scope.

fixtures.intent: Distinguish summed sender counts from unique conversations
fixtures.teaches: Summing correct per-sender counts can overstate the union.

fixtures.intent: Show why counts cannot estimate storage savings
fixtures.teaches: One declared large message can outweigh many small conversations; no real quota savings are inferred.

steps: Load the JSON using a standard JSON parser.
For mixed-age-starred, apply the stated message predicate, then take unique thread IDs. Compare both lists with expected.
For sender-wide-not-prior-query, calculate prior and sender-wide matches independently. Do not carry the prior predicate into the sender-wide predicate.
For overlapping-sender-counts, group unique thread IDs by sender, then compare their summed sizes with the union.
For count-versus-bytes, multiply the three declared fields for each group and compare sums and ratio.
Record local assertion results as synthetic arithmetic validation only. Do not label them live Gmail tests.

external_protocol.requires: Explicit authorization and a disposable test account; no mailbox setup or mutation is authorized by this file.
record: Installed product name, source, version, manifest/permissions, date, browser version, Gmail language and conversation-view setting.
Exact seeded synthetic message IDs, dates, stars, categories, folders and sender membership; confirm thread composition in UI.
Exact query, matching displayed conversations, open-thread contents, selection controls, confirmation wording and final action scope.
Any Trash test only after separate approval; before/after IDs and restoration verification, never permanent deletion for the protocol.
Elapsed human task time only with a defined start/end, repeated independent trials and failure accounting.
Account quota values and observation lag separately, if an authorized storage test is ever needed.

forbidden_inferences: No fixture proves Gmail search semantics beyond the linked documentation.
No fixture certifies installed-package identity, selector compatibility, exact counts, safety, scan speed, storage freed or competitor superiority.
